niagara-falls-from-the-american-side

The thundering Niagara Falls is seen from the American side, in a view with clouds of mist rising and a rainbow in the spray. Frederic Edwin Church returned to paint Niagara a decade after his first famous picture. The water seems to move in the painting. It's a different, cooler look at a famous wonder.
el-khasne-petra

The great rose-red temple of Petra in Jordan is carved into a cliff, with tiny people at its base. Church traveled to the Middle East in 1868 and visited Petra, a hidden city in the desert that few Westerners had seen. The painting shows the huge carved building glowing at sunrise. It's an adventure picture from a far-off place.
el-rio-de-luz

A broad river in South America shines in golden light, with misty green jungle and distant mountains. Church painted the 'River of Light' from his sketches in Ecuador. The warm glow of the sky is amazing. It's a luminous view of a faraway land.
cliff-dwellers

A crowded New York tenement street is full of kids, parents and laundry, in the dusty, bright light of summer. George Bellows painted the Lower East Side, a neighborhood full of immigrants, including many Jewish families. The crowded lives are painted with energy and warmth. It's a famous picture of the city's working-class life.
dempsey-and-firpo

A boxer is knocked out of the ring and thrown over the ropes into the crowd in a famous 1923 prizefight. George Bellows painted the dramatic moment in 1924 from memory. He loved sports, and painted several famous boxing scenes. It's one of the best-known American sports paintings.
fur-traders-descending-the-missouri

A fur trader and his young son glide down a misty river in a canoe, with a pet fox in the bow. George Caleb Bingham painted the quiet, golden river scene in 1845. The calm water and the glowing light made it one of the most loved paintings of the American frontier. It's a peaceful image of life on the river.
sha-co-pay-the-six-chief-of-the-plains-ojibwa

A portrait of an Ojibwe chief in splendid clothes and feathers. George Catlin traveled across the American West in the 1830s to paint Native Americans, because he feared their ways of life were disappearing. His paintings give a rare record of the people he met. It's a dignified portrait.
abraham-lincoln

President Abraham Lincoln, with his tall, thin face and deep eyes, is painted in a calm pose. George Peter Alexander Healy, an American painter, painted Lincoln from life in 1860 and made later copies. The portrait shows the kindness and sadness in the face. It's an important image of one of America's most beloved presidents.
the-skater

A tall, elegant man in a black coat and hat glides across an icy pond on one leg, in a graceful pose. Gilbert Stuart painted this portrait of William Grant in 1782 in London, and it made him famous. The picture shows the skater with a sense of fun. It hangs in the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
symphony-in-white-no-3

Two women in white dresses relax in a room, one on a sofa and the other sitting on the floor, with a fan and flowers. James McNeill Whistler, an American painter who lived in London, named his paintings like music. He cared more about harmony of color than about telling a story. It's a calm and elegant picture.
arrangement-in-grey-and-black-no-2-portrait-of-thomas-c

A grey-haired man in black sits in profile, looking down. Whistler painted the Scottish writer Thomas Carlyle in the same style as his famous portrait of his mother. Carlyle was one of Britain's leading thinkers. It's an important portrait with a simple, quiet beauty.
american-progress

A giant woman floating in the sky, with a book and a telegraph wire, leads settlers westward as buffalo and Native people flee into the darkness. John Gast painted this in 1872 as an advertisement for the idea of American expansion, called Manifest Destiny. Today people study it to understand both the pride and the pain of this period. It's one of the most famous pictures about the American West.
the-headless-horseman-pursuing-ichabod-crane

A skinny schoolmaster races on a horse as a headless rider chases him through a dark forest, throwing his pumpkin head. John Quidor painted this scene from Washington Irving's story 'The Legend of Sleepy Hollow'. His pictures are full of wild, funny movement. It's a spooky, thrilling American tale.
the-old-plantation

A group of enslaved people gather outdoors on a plantation in South Carolina, where some are dancing and playing music. This watercolor, painted in the 1780s, is one of the earliest pictures of African American life in the colonies. The musical instruments show African traditions that survived. It's an important historical record of enslaved people.
lady-with-the-rose

A young woman in a white dress holds a rose, painted with Sargent's smooth, quick brushwork. The sitter is Charlotte Louise Burckhardt. Sargent painted the picture in Paris in 1882. It's a graceful portrait from early in his career.
mrs-fiske-warren-gretchen-osgood-and-her-daughter-rache

A mother in a flowing red gown stands with her little girl, in front of a rich background. John Singer Sargent painted wealthy Boston families like the Warrens. His brush made the satin and lace shimmer. It's a lovely portrait of mother and child.
surrender-of-general-burgoyne

In October 1777, the British General Burgoyne surrenders his army to the American General Gates after the battle of Saratoga, a turning point in the American Revolution. John Trumbull painted the scene as part of his set of Revolution paintings for the U.S. Capitol. The picture shows the first great American victory. It hangs in the Capitol Rotunda.
landing-of-columbus

Columbus steps ashore in the New World, with the Spanish flag, as sailors kneel and Native people watch from the forest. John Vanderlyn painted this huge scene for the U.S. Capitol Rotunda. Today, many people see the story of Columbus in a different light. It's a famous American history painting.
approaching-thunder-storm

A black storm approaches over a calm bay as the sky grows dark and the water glows eerily. Martin Johnson Heade painted this in 1859, with a sense of drama right before the storm. A lone sailboat is the only sign of people. It's one of the most mysterious American paintings.
in-the-loge

A woman in a black dress looks through binoculars from a theater box, while someone in the audience might be looking back at her. Mary Cassatt, an American painter in Paris, painted women as people who looked at the world, not just as objects to be looked at. The picture is full of clever ideas. It hangs in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
lady-at-the-tea-table

A woman in a dark dress sits at a tea table with a gleaming silver and porcelain tea service. Mary Cassatt painted her cousin, Mrs. Riddle, who didn't like the portrait at all. The painting is now seen as one of Cassatt's best. It's an elegant picture of ritual.
mother-and-child-the-oval-mirror

A mother holds her child on her lap, and a round mirror hangs behind them. Mary Cassatt became famous for her pictures of mothers and children. The soft colors and gentle gestures show a close bond. It's one of her most tender works.
woman-with-a-sunflower

A young woman in a bright dress holds a sunflower in a garden, painted with bright strokes. Mary Cassatt painted this late in her career, with a bold, colorful touch. The sunflower is glowing. It's a lovely, joyful portrait.
afternoon-tea

Women in long, pale dresses sit and take tea in a sunlit room, in a soft and dreamy style. Richard Edward Miller was an American Impressionist who spent time in the art colony at Giverny, France, where Monet lived. The light is gentle and warm. It's a pretty, relaxed picture.
kaaterskill-falls

A waterfall plunges through a wild forest in the Catskill Mountains of New York, with a small figure in the foreground. Thomas Cole, the founder of the Hudson River School, painted this in 1826 when he was a young artist. The painting made him famous. It's a landmark in American landscape painting.
view-of-florence

The city of Florence, Italy, shines golden in the setting sun, seen from a hill. Thomas Cole lived in Florence for a while, learning from the great Italian art. The soft light and the city's domes are lovely. It's a peaceful travel picture.
the-fountain-of-vaucluse

A scene in southern France, near a spring that is the source of a river, with cliffs, a castle and a lone traveler. Thomas Cole was inspired by the poet Petrarch, who lived here. The romantic landscape is full of mystery. It's a poetic picture.
arch-of-nero

An ancient Roman arch stands in ruins in a landscape in Italy, in the golden light of evening. Thomas Cole loved to paint the ruins of the ancient world. The quiet ruins remind us that great empires fade. It's a thoughtful, romantic landscape.
cross-at-sunset

A tall wooden cross stands on a hillside in a glowing sunset, with a lake below. Thomas Cole, born in England and raised in America, painted this landscape with a feeling of faith. The calm, golden light is moving. It's a quiet, spiritual picture.
portrait-of-professor-benjamin-h-rand

A man in a dark suit sits in a chair, with a serious face and a book. Thomas Eakins painted his friend, Professor Rand, a doctor and a teacher at Jefferson Medical College in Philadelphia. The dark colors and honest face show Eakins's realism. It's a thoughtful portrait of a scientist.
miss-amelia-van-buren

A woman sits in a chair, looking a bit tired or sad, in a dim room. Thomas Eakins painted this quiet portrait, and the sitter's honest face is typical of his work. It hangs in the Phillips Collection in Washington. It's a famous portrait for its honesty.
a-rose

A single pink rose is painted in the soft light of an afternoon. Thomas Pollock Anshutz was a Philadelphia painter and teacher who taught many famous artists at the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts. He painted this late in his career. It's a delicate, gentle still life.
breezing-up

Four people in a small sailboat lean back as the wind fills the sails and the boat dashes across a sparkling sea, with a few clouds. Winslow Homer, one of America's greatest painters, painted this in 1876 (originally called 'A Fair Wind'). The fresh air and speed feel real. It's one of the best-loved American paintings.
the-fog-warning

A fisherman in a small dory looks anxiously at a bank of fog rolling in as he rows toward his ship, with a catch of halibut. Winslow Homer painted it in 1885 in Maine. The big waves and the long distance to the ship make you hold your breath. It's a famous picture of danger at sea.
fox-hunt

A fox runs across a deep snowy field while a flock of hungry crows swoops down to attack it. Winslow Homer painted this in 1893 at his home on the coast of Maine. The winter scene is both beautiful and harsh. It's one of the most dramatic animal paintings in American art.
the-gulf-stream

A Black sailor lies on the deck of a broken boat, surrounded by sharks, as a waterspout twists in the distance and a ship sails far away. Winslow Homer painted this in 1899, after traveling to the Caribbean. The painting makes people wonder whether he will be saved. It's one of his most famous and powerful works.
reminiscence-of-the-tempyo-era

A woman in the elegant clothes of the 8th-century Tempyō era of Japan, painted in a Western oil style. Fujishima Takeji was a Japanese painter who studied in Europe and brought back new ideas. The painting mixes Japan's ancient past with a modern style. It's a famous picture from Meiji-era Japan.
guanyin-riding-the-dragon

A calm Buddhist figure, Guanyin, stands on a roaring dragon above clouds and waves. Harada Naojirō was a Japanese artist who studied in Germany and painted in the Western style. The painting mixes ancient Asian subjects with modern oil painting. It's a striking meeting of East and West.
autumn-millet-and-sparrows

Sparrows cling to a bending stalk of autumn millet, painted with great care for every feather and seed. Itō Jakuchū was an eccentric Japanese painter in Kyoto who owned a vegetable shop and raised chickens to study them. He is now celebrated as one of Japan's greatest painters of animals. It's a delightful close-up of nature.
elephant-and-whale

A huge white elephant on one folding screen and a giant whale on the other face each other across the two sides, like a big playful puzzle. Itō Jakuchū painted them in 1795 in a dotted, quirky style that looks like a pixel picture. The two giants, one of land and one of sea, seem to say hello. It's a fun, funny masterpiece of Japanese art.
bugaku-dances-and-music

Dancers in colorful costume and masks perform the ancient court dance called bugaku, as musicians play. Kanō Eigaku painted the scene in a classic Japanese style with fine details. Bugaku has been performed in Japan for over a thousand years. It's a lively picture of traditional performance.
the-great-wave-off-kanagawa

A giant wave curls over like a claw above three small fishing boats, with Mount Fuji tiny and calm in the distance. Katsushika Hokusai made this woodblock print around 1831 when he was about 70, and it became the most famous image of Japanese art in the world. Thousands of copies were printed, and it inspired artists in Europe like Van Gogh and Monet. It's a perfect picture of nature's power.
fine-wind-clear-morning

Mount Fuji glows red in the morning sun, with white clouds drifting and a deep blue sky. Hokusai made this woodblock print, called 'Red Fuji,' as part of his series Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji. The mountain looks big and calm, like a friendly giant. It's one of the most beloved prints from Japan.
kajikazawa-in-kai-province

A fisherman stands on a rock in the swirling sea with a net, as Mount Fuji rises in the distance. This woodblock print by Hokusai shows him pulling a line against the rolling waves. The simple shapes are very bold. It's part of his series of Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji.
under-the-mannen-bridge-at-fukagawa

A water bucket hangs from a rope under a tall bridge over a canal, with Mount Fuji in the circle of the arch. Hokusai made this clever woodblock print, a view framed in a tricky way. The strong curve of the bridge is dramatic. It's a fun surprise when you spot Fuji.
lightnings-below-the-summit

A black storm and lightning bolts flash at the foot of Mount Fuji while the peak stays bright and calm above. Hokusai's woodblock print is nicknamed 'Black Fuji' in a companion to the 'Red Fuji.' The peak stands above the weather. It's a dramatic image of a peaceful mountain.
lake-suwa-in-shinano-province

A tiny shrine on a rock sits in a lake, with Mount Fuji far away across the water. Hokusai created this woodblock print as part of his famous series of Fuji views. The calm lake and old pines are peaceful. It's a quiet scene in the middle of a famous series.
sundai-edo

People in the city of Edo (now Tokyo) look at Mount Fuji from a hilltop, over the rooftops, with a street full of people. Hokusai made this woodblock print to show the mountain near the busy city. Fuji is small but present. It's a friendly picture of everyday life.
fujimigahara-in-owari-province

Workers building a huge barrel, with Mount Fuji tiny in the middle of the circle of the barrel. Hokusai made this clever woodblock print by framing the mountain inside the round barrel. It's a playful trick that shows his humor. It's one of the most charming prints in the series.
founding-of-the-nation

Gods and goddesses from Japanese legend stand in a misty sky above the sea, creating the islands of Japan with a jeweled spear. Kawamura Kiyoo painted this in a Western oil style, showing the old Shinto myth of the creation of Japan. The story says the god Izanagi and the goddess Izanami stirred the sea with a spear. It's a major painting from Japan's Meiji era.
actor-ichikawa-shiko-as-kato-yomoshichi

A kabuki actor in a bold costume strikes a dramatic pose in a woodblock print. Konishi Hirosada was a printmaker in Osaka who made prints of famous actors. Fans collected such prints like trading cards. It's a picture of a Japanese theater star.
the-ghost-of-oyuki

A pale ghost woman with long black hair, in a white robe, floats in the air with no feet. Maruyama Ōkyo, a Japanese painter from Kyoto, is said to have started the style of painting ghosts without legs. Japanese ghost stories are very popular, and this ghost is one of the most famous. It's a spooky and beautiful image.
morning-glories-and-puppies

Puppies play under a trellis of morning glories in the soft light of dawn. Maruyama Ōkyo was famous for painting animals from life, which was new in Japan, and his puppies are a famous example. The soft fluffy dogs have made many people smile. It's an adorable picture from the 1700s.
